items.followUp: What is the role of bile in digestion?

rubric.why: HCl creates the acidic conditions needed for pepsin and activates pepsinogen.
rubric.description: States a function of HCl in the stomach.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that HCl provides an acidic medium or activates pepsinogen.

rubric.why: Pepsin is the enzyme that digests proteins in the stomach.
rubric.description: States the substrate and products of pepsin digestion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that pepsin digests proteins into peptides or peptones.

modelAnswer: HCl provides an acidic medium in the stomach and activates pepsinogen into pepsin.
Pepsin digests proteins into simpler substances such as peptides or peptones.

items.followUp: What is goitre, and what can cause it?

rubric.why: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to make thyroxine.
rubric.description: Connects iodine deficiency with reduced thyroid hormone production.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that iodine is required to produce thyroxine or thyroid hormone.

rubric.why: Iodine deficiency can cause enlargement of the thyroid gland, known as goitre.
rubric.description: Identifies thyroid enlargement or goitre as an effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming goitre or describing enlargement/swelling of the thyroid gland.

modelAnswer: Iodine is required by the thyroid gland to produce thyroxine; iodine deficiency reduces thyroxine production.
The thyroid gland may enlarge, causing goitre.

items.followUp: How can excessive transpiration affect a plant?

rubric.why: Excessive transpiration can remove water faster than the roots replace it.
rubric.description: Explains the water-loss effect of excessive transpiration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that transpiration causes excessive water loss or that water loss exceeds absorption.

rubric.why: Severe water loss causes wilting and can eventually kill the plant.
rubric.description: States a harmful consequence of excessive water loss.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning wilting or possible death of the plant.

modelAnswer: If transpiration is excessive, water may be lost faster than it is absorbed by the roots.
This causes the plant to wilt and, in severe cases, may lead to its death.

items.followUp: How can red blood cells and white blood cells be separated from blood?

rubric.why: Centrifugation separates blood components according to their density.
rubric.description: Names the method used to separate plasma from blood.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming centrifugation or use of a centrifuge.

rubric.why: The denser blood cells settle below the less dense plasma during centrifugation.
rubric.description: Describes the positions of the separated blood cells and plasma.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the cells settle at the bottom while plasma remains in the upper layer.

modelAnswer: Blood is placed in a tube and centrifuged.
The denser blood cells settle at the bottom, while plasma remains as the upper layer (supernatant).

items.followUp: Compare the functions of chloroplasts and leucoplasts.

rubric.why: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
rubric.description: Explains the pigment and function of chloroplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking chlorophyll in chloroplasts with photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Pigments in chromoplasts give colour to plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that chromoplasts contain pigments or impart colour.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids involved in food storage.
rubric.description: Identifies leucoplasts as colourless or as food-storing plastids.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either characteristic or function.

rubric.why: Starch, oil and protein are examples of substances stored by leucoplasts.
rubric.description: Names a food substance stored by leucoplasts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming starch, oil or protein as a stored substance.

modelAnswer: Chloroplasts are green plastids containing chlorophyll; they carry out photosynthesis.
Chromoplasts contain coloured pigments and give colour to flowers, fruits and other plant parts.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food such as starch, oil or protein.

items.followUp: State five characteristics of enzymes and explain why temperature affects their activity.

rubric.why: Enzymes are biological catalysts and are generally proteins; these are two valid characteristics.
rubric.description: Identifies enzymes as catalysts and as proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the catalyst role and 1 mark for stating that enzymes are proteins.

rubric.why: Specificity, effectiveness in small amounts and reusability are further enzyme characteristics.
rubric.description: States two further characteristics of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for each of two distinct characteristics, such as substrate specificity, acting in small amounts, or remaining unchanged and being reusable.

rubric.why: Enzyme activity depends on temperature, and excessive heat can denature enzymes.
rubric.description: States a valid temperature-related characteristic of enzymes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that activity depends on temperature, identifying an optimum temperature, or explaining that high temperatures denature enzymes.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts and are generally proteins.
Each enzyme is specific to its substrate or reaction.
Enzymes can act in small amounts and remain unchanged after a reaction, so they can be reused.
Enzyme activity is affected by temperature, and each enzyme works best at an optimum temperature.
High temperatures can denature an enzyme and reduce or stop its activity.
